newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: POSSIBLE DEAL AGREED IN WOOLWORTHS STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: POSSIBLE DEAL AGREED IN WOOLWORTHS STRIKE.

text.p: A striking union at South Africa's Woolworths, a unit of stores group Wooltru, have reached a proposed agreement to settle the dispute, the firm said on Friday.
Woolworths said it had met with representatives of the South African Commercial, Catering and Allied Workers Union (SACCAWU) on Thursday and come up with a possible settlement.

Woolworths is offering an across the board pay rise of 260 rand a month taking the average monthly salary to 2,888 rand. The union has accepted management plans to meet a rising pattern of weekend shopping in the country.
The plan includes greater staff flexibility and multi-tasking.
SACCAWU is to report back to its members and has a deadline of Monday, August 11, to confirm the deal.
Woolworths said the two parties had also agreed that if striking or picketing activity took place during the report back period the offer would be withdrawn.
Woolworths has said it has traded normally during the strike as the balance of its 10,000 employees were not taking part in the action.

The settlement talks were brokered by the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration, a body set up under the terms of South Africa's new Labour Relations Act to provide fast mediation of labour disputes.
